A1.justification: Despite the changed title and NF/HNF-to-IKF/HNS terminology, both PDFs describe the same kernel-integral Hamiltonian solver. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original functional-fitting experiments, Advection/KdV/SWE simulations, Hamiltonian-conservation analyses, inductive-bias ablations and inference timings.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluated baselines, architecture ablations, training-data-size studies, discretization tests and numerical-solver timings.

M1.justification: The evaluated kernel architecture, gradient-training objective and Adams–Bashforth inference procedure remain unchanged. New Appendix C.3 proposes coefficient-conditioned inputs or output scaling, and source-field inputs or additive gradient corrections. These are proposed procedural extensions, without corresponding experimental validation.

E1.justification: The toy functionals and three PDE families remain. Appendix B.5 adds spatial-domain extrapolation for Advection, testing on [0,32] after training on [0,16], extending the evaluated input conditions. The coefficient and bathymetry cases in C.3 are derivations, not additional evaluated datasets.

E2.justification: PINO and Transolver, previously only cited, become evaluated SWE comparators in Table 3 and Figure 4, adding physics-informed and attention-based comparisons. Table 6 also adds analytical/numerical solver timing comparisons. Existing MLP, FNO and Unet comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark splits, metrics and numerical integration settings are retained. New B.3–B.5 introduce cumulative architecture controls with approximately matched parameter counts, training subsets from one-eighth to full size, and resolution tests using downsampled or re-solved validation labels. B.2 adds CPU solver timing averaged over ten samples, substantially extending the evaluation design.

E4.justification: The existing Hamiltonian-error and inductive-bias analyses remain. New B.3 tests kernel nonlinearity, conditioning, SIREN architecture and receptive field; B.4 tests training-data requirements; B.5 tests resolution and spatial-domain generalization. Table 7's caption ambiguously includes SIREN in the base model despite a subsequent '+ SIREN' row.

E5.justification: The reported seed count for 1D PDE results increases from three to six. Table 1 newly specifies averages over six seeds; v1 did not state its toy-experiment run count. SWE results retain three-seed mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, and no new significance-testing framework is introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 2 contain revised estimates alongside changed seed reporting. For example, KdV Unet correlation time changes from 125.7 to 134.0, while derivative-Unet changes from 127.4 to 113.3. Original SWE comparator scores remain unchanged, but PINO/Transolver scores, solver timings, architecture/data-size/discretization results and revised plotted examples substantially expand the reported evidence.

T1.justification: The original linear-approximation proof is retained. New C.2 develops gradient expressions connecting global nonlinear kernels to cylindrical approximation, and C.3 derives coefficient/source-term extensions. However, Eqs. 26–28 are internally inconsistent: applying J to the added ghb term differentiates h as well as b, so it does not recover the stated bathymetry source term.

C1.justification: v1 claims a first architecture for learning function-to-scalar mappings. v2 explicitly builds on previous functional approximators and centers the contribution on Hamiltonian PDE solvers, functional-derivative learning and neural-field parameterization. The central accuracy, conservation and temporal/OOD generalization claims are retained.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of PINO as soft regularization, differing data requirements across PDEs, and architecture-dependent resolution/domain generalization. It also develops a cylindrical-approximation explanation, discusses case-dependent coefficient/source extensions, and adds quadrature-scalability concerns and qualifications about hardware and accuracy matching in solver timing comparisons.

D1.justification: v2 specifies the numerical-solver CPU, explains the lack of GPU compatibility, and distinguishes PyClaw's Fortran implementation from the Python KdV solver. Its checklist points to configuration files, while Table 1 removes the approximate 30-second toy-training estimate. The repository disclosure, core hyperparameter tables and numerical implementation instructions are retained.

R1.justification: A dedicated Functional Approximation discussion acknowledges neural integral functionals, parameter-to-observable maps, functional autoencoders and generative neural operators. Additional discussion connects the work to density-functional theory and cylindrical approximation. This substantially revises the research positioning and replaces the blanket function-to-scalar architecture priority claim.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and framing paragraphs are revised, and NF/HNF terminology largely becomes IKF/HNS. Related Works moves before a consolidated Conclusion containing Limitations and Outlook; appendices gain subsections and a checklist. Most background, core method and retained experimental prose remains closely matched, so the editorial reworking is limited relative to the substantive additions.

P2.justification: Figures 2–7 are redrawn or reformatted with changed legends, colors, scales or example trajectories; Figure 4 adds comparator curves. Tables 3 and 6 expand, and three new multi-experiment tables present architecture, dataset-size and discretization studies. The original hyperparameter tables are retained as Tables 10–12.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important attribution and validation weaknesses: it replaces the broad architecture-priority claim with explicit recognition of predecessors and adds relevant comparators, controlled ablations, generalization studies and increased 1D replication. These substantially strengthen the retained solver's empirical case. The inconsistent Table 7 caption and incorrect bathymetry source-term recovery in C.3 weaken particular additions, but do not outweigh the improvements to the central contribution's positioning and support.
